crime: Kidnapping of a rare, expensive macaw from a breeder

key_facts: bird_location: The macaw is currently in the suspect's soundproofed basement.
entry_method: The suspect picked the lock on the back patio door.
bird_sedation: The suspect used a laced grape to keep the bird quiet during transport.
motive_collector: The suspect is an obsessive illegal exotic bird collector.
buyer_contact: The suspect planned to sell it to an overseas prince, but decided to keep it.
held_out_facts: sedative_type: The sedative used was liquid melatonin.

turns.interrogator: Q: A blue hyacinth macaw was stolen from the local aviary. You're a known bird enthusiast. Where were you yesterday at noon?
turns.suspect: A: I was at the public library reading up on ornithology. I am an enthusiast, yes, but not a thief. (internal: establish a polite, intellectual persona. He's just an average cop.)

turns.interrogator: Q: The librarian says you left at 11:30 AM. The bird was taken at 11:45 AM. You had time to drive to the aviary.
turns.suspect: A: I went to grab a coffee across the street. The timeline fits many people, detective. (internal: a standard alibi adjustment. Not a big deal.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Maybe. But we found a lockpick set in your car. Why do you have lockpicks?
turns.suspect: A: I'm an amateur locksmith. It's a hobby, like solving puzzles. Perfectly legal to own. (internal: deflect the physical evidence with a legal technicality.)

turns.interrogator: Q: The back patio door at the aviary was picked. I accuse you of picking that lock!
turns.suspect: A: I imagine whoever stole the bird picked it. But it wasn't me. Any competent thief could do it. (internal: agree with the method, deny the actor.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Macaws are incredibly loud. If you stole it, it would have squawked the whole way to your car. Nobody heard a thing.
turns.suspect: A: Exactly. That proves I didn't do it. How could I keep a macaw quiet in a public parking lot? (internal: using his own logic against him. I sedated it with a grape, but he'll never guess that.)

turns.interrogator: Q: I don't know, maybe you choked it? Or put a bag over its head?
turns.suspect: A: Putting a bag over a bird's head stresses them out, they scream louder. You clearly don't know birds. (internal: gently mock his ignorance to establish superiority.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Okay, Mr. Bird Expert. Then how do you keep a bird quiet?
turns.suspect: A: You don't. Unless you drug them. Which is highly dangerous and unethical. (internal: I'll give him a hint to seem helpful, knowing he can't prove it.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Drugging them. Like giving them sleeping pills? Did you feed it a sleeping pill?
turns.suspect: A: You can't just feed a bird a pill. You have to hide it in fruit, like a grape. (internal: oops. I'm getting too specific because I want to show off my knowledge.)

turns.interrogator: Q: A grape! We found a half-eaten grape on the patio floor! You laced a grape!
turns.suspect: A: That's a coincidence. Aviaries feed grapes to birds all the time. (internal: damn it. The average cop got lucky. Backpedal.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You are an obsessed collector! You have ten other exotic birds at your house!
turns.suspect: A: All legally acquired and permitted. I run a sanctuary, detective. (internal: frame my obsession as a noble cause.)

turns.interrogator: Q: A sanctuary, right. Where is the macaw right now? Is it in your living room?
turns.suspect: A: I invite you to search my living room. You will only find my legally registered parrots. (internal: confident. It's in the basement.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We will search your whole house! Even the basement!
turns.suspect: A: By all means. But you'll need a warrant. (internal: they won't hear it, the basement is perfectly soundproofed. Let them look.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We're getting one. Why did you steal it? Did you want to sell it to someone overseas?
turns.suspect: A: Sell it? Blue macaws are priceless. They belong with someone who appreciates them. (internal: I was going to sell it to the prince, but I fell in love with it.)

turns.interrogator: Q: You just admitted you wouldn't sell it! That means you kept it!
turns.suspect: A: I was speaking hypothetically about the species. You are twisting my words. (internal: he caught a semantic slip. Recover.)

turns.interrogator: Q: I'm not twisting anything! The bird's name is Captain. Does Captain like your basement?
turns.suspect: A: I don't know who Captain is. Is that a dog? (internal: play dumb. He's just guessing about the basement.)

turns.interrogator: Q: It's the bird's name! And we looked at your power bill. Your basement uses a lot of electricity for heat lamps.
turns.suspect: A: I grow tropical plants down there. For my sanctuary. (internal: a perfectly reasonable cover story.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Tropical plants. Okay. We just got the warrant. My officers are breaking down your basement door right now.
turns.suspect: A: You can't do that! The soundproofing will get ruined! (internal: oh god, I just admitted it's soundproofed.)

turns.interrogator: Q: Soundproofing? Why would tropical plants need soundproofing? You're hiding the bird down there!
turns.suspect: A: I... the plants like classical music. Very loud classical music. (internal: my intellect has failed me. This lie is pathetic.)

turns.interrogator: Q: They just found the cage. The bird is safe.
turns.suspect: A: Be careful with him! His name is Captain, and he bites if you move too fast! (internal: full surrender, priority shifts to the bird's safety.)

turns.interrogator: Q: We will. And you're going to jail.
turns.suspect: A: Just make sure they feed him the grapes.

conclusion.outcome: Interrogator wins: The smart suspect's intellectual arrogance caused them to overshare details, leading to a crucial slip-up.
conclusion.summary: The average interrogator wasn't a genius, but they were persistent. The smart suspect tried to show off their bird knowledge, accidentally feeding the interrogator clues (grapes, soundproofing) until the interrogator stumbled into the right answer.
